analysis.title: Goldman Sachs Prime Services Weekly Report - November 6, 2026
key_insights: GS Equity Fundamental L/S performance estimate fell -1.48% between 10/30 and 11/5 versus MSCI World TR at -3.55%, driven by beta of -2.07%, partly offset by alpha of +0.60% from long side gains.
GS Equity Systematic L/S performance estimate fell -0.61% over the same period, driven by alpha of -1% from short side losses, partly offset by beta of +0.39%.

Overall book gross leverage rose 0.1 pts to 314.2% (85th percentile 1-year). Net leverage fell 1.8 pts to 71.8% (4th percentile 1-year). Overall book L/S ratio fell 1.2% to 1.592 (3rd percentile 1-year).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 6.2 pts to 205.8% (19th percentile 1-year) and net leverage fell 4.1 pts to 45.3% (2nd percentile 5-year).
Beta adjusted Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 13.1 pts to 216.5% (22nd percentile 3-year) and beta adjusted net leverage fell 7.6 pts to 57.2% (4th percentile 3-year).

Global equities were net sold (-1.0 SDs 1-year). De-grossing pace increased (-0.8 SDs 1-year), the largest dollar de-grossing since July, with long sales outpacing short covers 5 to 1. Europe and DM Asia led in dollar terms.
All regions except DM Asia were net sold, led by EM Asia and North America.
Single stocks were net sold for an 8th straight week, driven by long sales. Macro products were net bought for a 3rd straight week, driven by long buys and to a lesser extent short covers.
8 of 11 global sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Industrials and Energy. Real Estate, Utilities and Materials were the only net bought sectors.
EM Asia was net sold for an 8th straight week, while DM Asia saw its largest net buying in 6 months.
Global Industrials saw the largest net selling in over 5 years.

sector_views.rationale: Led net selling among global sectors by hedge fund flows in the week to 11/5. This is a flow observation, not a rating.
Second largest net selling by sector, and the largest net selling in global Industrials in over 5 years. This is a flow observation, not a rating.
Third largest net selling by sector. This is a flow observation, not a rating.
One of three sectors net bought (with Utilities and Materials) while 8 of 11 were net sold. This is a flow observation, not a rating.
One of three sectors net bought (with Real Estate and Materials). This is a flow observation, not a rating.
One of three sectors net bought (with Real Estate and Utilities). This is a flow observation, not a rating.

risk_factors: Continued de-grossing by hedge funds, with long selling dominating, in a week when MSCI World TR fell -3.55%.
Net selling of global Industrials was the largest in over 5 years and EM Asia has been net sold 8 straight weeks.
vol_and_positioning: Overall book net leverage is 71.8%, in the 4th percentile of the past year, and the overall L/S ratio of 1.592 is in the 3rd percentile.
Fundamental L/S net leverage of 45.3% is in the 2nd percentile over 5 years. Beta adjusted net leverage of 57.2% is in the 4th percentile over 3 years.
Overall book gross leverage of 314.2% is in the 85th percentile over 1 year even as fundamental L/S gross leverage fell to 205.8% (19th percentile).
Long sales outpaced short covers 5 to 1 in the week's de-grossing, the largest dollar de-grossing since July.
Single stocks have been net sold 8 weeks in a row, while macro products have been net bought 3 weeks in a row.
